note: [agent-bulk] The biggest object in my shard and it is well reconstructed. shw 23018 (1155.6 MeV, 42 seg, 286.4 cm, conn 1, nuecc) starts ON the vertex - the X and the blue star coincide on shw23018-az+085-el+20 - and both azimuths show the same thing: a narrow stem out of the star, then the shower blossoming into a wide branching cone with a dense point cloud, then a sparse tail of stubs out to ~137 cm. One apex, one direction, the yellow halo covering the whole branching structure including all the far stubs. Nothing is missing where it matters: the acceptance plot has steps at 25 deg to 80 cm, 12.5 deg from 80-130 cm and 5 deg beyond, and ALL FOUR non-member circles fall OUTSIDE those boxes - (23 cm, 26.5 deg) just above the 25 deg step, (84.5 cm, 22.5 deg) and (115 cm, 23.8 deg) above the 12.5 deg step, (137.5 cm, 7.5 deg) above the 5 deg step. The algorithm's own geometry rejected each of them and I agree with each rejection on the pictures. The one thing I considered and decided against calling under-clustering: at dist 0 / angle 0, in the shower's own cluster 23, sit 23019 (4.65 cm, pdg 13, owned by NOBODY) and 23020 (2.96 cm, its own sub-20 MeV shower) - grey pieces right at the shower start. For a nuecc that is vertex hadronic activity beside the electron, and keeping it out of the electron shower is what the reconstruction should do, so I read those exclusions as correct rather than as a hole. Also examined: shw 25060 (206.7 MeV, 4 seg, 32.8 cm), 98.8 cm from 23018 at 82 deg - a compact bent object inside its own dense cluster-25 point cloud, with nothing unclaimed in its cone (nearest non-members 89102 at 11.9 cm / 54.3 deg and 91104 at 46 cm / 45.8 deg); it reads fine. NOT examined: shw 86094 (41.8 MeV, 1 seg) and shw 93106 (15.8 cm, 386 cm away in a different region of the detector), plus the 21 showers skipped by the <20 MeV rule - so this is a claim about 2 showers of 25, not about the event. No reco pi0 (pio_grp=0, every pio_id=-1); the capture's pio slots [23018, 25060] were filled by the tool, not by the reconstruction. The vtx-* sweep is half-span 400 cm (that 386 cm outlier shower sets it) so it was useless for anything but gross topology and I judged entirely off the auto-framed shower frames. Verdict is about clustering and silent on PID.
